TabICL: 50 paired repetitions with Y-only MCAR

The experiment generates 50 independent datasets, each with 160 records. Exactly 32 values of Y are hidden under MCAR in each dataset. X, A and B remain fully observed and unchanged. The same data, mask and model seed are used for all three methods within each repetition. Only hidden Y values contribute to the scores.

X ~ Normal(0,1)
A sampled independently from {A,B}; B from {B,C}
Y | X,A,B ~ Normal(mu[A,B] + 4*X, 0.5^2)
mu[A,B] = -8, -2, 2, 10 for (A,B), (A,C), (B,B), (B,C)

Fine-tuning uses a maximum of 20 epochs, learning rate 1e-5, patience three and eight inference ensemble members. The sequential variant permits up to ten sweeps with the normal convergence rule. Parameters are fixed in advance; hidden values are never used for model selection. The default VIM learner still uses five epochs outside this experiment.

The base data seed is 20261016 + 100*(repetition - 1); masking uses seed + 1 and the shared R model seed is seed + 2. The Python learner random_state remains fixed at 42 across repetitions. Original data, masks and completions are retained in the local repetition cache. config.rds records the full configuration and source-file fingerprints; run-info.txt records the source commit. No repetitions are selected based on their results.

RMSE distributions across paired repetitions

Paired comparisons

Differences below are second method minus first method, so negative values favor the second method. Confidence intervals use the variation of within-repetition differences, preserving the paired design. Wins use an absolute RMSE difference greater than 1e-8; smaller differences are ties.

First Second Mean RMSE difference 95% MC CI Second wins Ties First wins
Pretrained Fine-tuned -0.0003 [-0.0066, 0.0060] 13 23 14
Pretrained Fine-tuned sequential -0.0112 [-0.0185, -0.0038] 31 0 19
Fine-tuned Fine-tuned sequential -0.0109 [-0.0174, -0.0043] 33 0 17

Fine-tuning alone changed mean RMSE by only −0.0003; its paired 95% interval includes zero. It improved RMSE in 13 repetitions, worsened it in 14, and tied in 23. Sequential fine-tuning reduced mean RMSE by 0.0112 (2.0%) relative to pretrained TabICL, with a paired 95% interval of [−0.0185, −0.0038]. It improved RMSE in 31 of 50 repetitions. All sequential runs stopped after three sweeps under the convergence rule; seq=10 is the maximum number of sweeps.

Paired RMSE differences with 95% Monte Carlo intervals

These are pointwise Monte Carlo intervals for this data-generating process, sample size and missingness protocol. They do not establish superiority on other datasets or missingness mechanisms. A missing value in the accuracy CSV field means classification accuracy is inapplicable to numeric Y, not an unfilled target.

Workers ran in separate R/Python processes with one Torch/BLAS thread each. The larger UCI benchmark was running concurrently, so elapsed times describe this run rather than isolated hardware performance. Initial model loading and caching also affect runtime comparisons.

The sequential method receives no newly imputed predictors in this Y-only scenario. Any difference from one pass reflects refitting rather than recovery of missing predictor information. Lower point RMSE does not by itself establish better distribution preservation or proper multiple imputation.

Reproducibility

Raw repetition artifacts stay in .local/benchmarks/tabicl2-correlated-y-only-typed-epochs20-50reps/. The accompanying metrics.csv contains all 150 method/repetition rows; summary.csv and paired.csv contain the displayed statistics.
